title: House Floor Debate
subtitle: H.R.6001 — Social Security 2100: A Sacred Trust Act

metadata.laymanSummary: A bill to strengthen Social Security for 75 years by raising the payroll tax cap on high earners narrowly failed in the House, despite polling showing 80% public support for the measure.

data.billTitle: Social Security 2100: A Sacred Trust Act — Raising payroll tax cap on earnings over $400K to extend solvency through 2100

speakers.name: Rep. John Larson
speakers.title: D-CT · House Ways and Means
speakers.quote: Social Security will be insolvent in eight years without action. Eight years. That means a 23% across-the-board benefit cut for 70 million Americans — including veterans, the disabled, and every retiree in this country. This bill asks people who earn more than $400,000 a year to contribute to the program that kept their grandparents out of poverty. That is not radical. That is arithmetic.

speakers.name: Rep. Hakeem Jeffries
speakers.title: D-NY · House Minority Leader
speakers.quote: Franklin Roosevelt called Social Security a sacred trust. We are in this chamber today because Republicans would rather cut benefits than ask billionaires to pay the same Social Security tax rate as a schoolteacher. A teacher in Connecticut pays Social Security taxes on every dollar she earns. Jeff Bezos stops paying after his first $160,000. That is the system Republicans want to protect.

speakers.name: Rep. Mike Johnson
speakers.title: R-LA · House Speaker
speakers.quote: Social Security faces a structural math problem. Raising taxes on job creators does not fix the math — it damages the economy that funds Social Security. We need to modernize the program through sensible reforms to the retirement age and benefit calculations that reflect a 2026 life expectancy, not a 1935 one. Tax hikes are not reform. They are delay.

data.title: What This Vote Means
data.text: H.R.6001 failed 208-225. The bill would have extended Social Security solvency to 2100 by applying the payroll tax to wages above $400,000 (currently capped at $168,600), increasing benefits by roughly $200/month, and creating a new minimum benefit of 125% of the poverty line. The Social Security Trustees project the Trust Fund will be depleted by 2033 without action, triggering automatic 23% benefit cuts.
